subject: can this be made more default-y?

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: can this be made more default-y?
parts:
Hi--when I run Stan from R, I see this:

> library("rstan")
Loading required package: ggplot2
Loading required package: StanHeaders
rstan (Version 2.11.1, packaged: 2016-07-28 18:19:31 UTC, GitRev: 85f7a56811da)
For execution on a local, multicore CPU with excess RAM we recommend calling
rstan_options(auto_write = TRUE)
options(mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())

--

So then I put the following lines in my script:

library("rstan")
rstan_options(auto_write = TRUE)
options(mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())

--

But I've noticed that users often don't know about this. I've been told that for some reason we can't make those two lines automatic, but could we at least make them easier to do? Maybe some option in the stan() call or something, or a function stan_fast() or something like that? I really hate to think about all those users who are (a) recompiling their model every time, and (b) running in serial, when they could be running in parallel 4 times as fast!

A

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: can this be made more default-y?
parts:
If a user wants to automate that, he/she can add the following to their .Rprofile file ($HOME/.Rprofile):

setHook(packageEvent("rstan", "onLoad"), function(...) {

  rstan::rstan_options(auto_write = TRUE)

  options(mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())

})


I have no real opinion on this, but the changes are visible by the time RStan's .onAttach is run so that startup messages can be modified, perhaps to check if the options are already set and/or spit out instructions about modifying one's profile. E.g., running:


profileFile <- file.path(Sys.getenv("HOME"), ".Rprofile")

if (!file.exists(profileFile)) file.create(profileFile)

cat("\nsetHook(packageEvent(\"rstan\", \"onLoad\"), function(...) {",

    "  rstan::rstan_options(auto_write = TRUE)",

    "  options(mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())",

    "})\n", sep = "\n", file = profileFile, append = TRUE)
